narrativeReportMd:
# Encounter R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
Breaking changes were found. Encounter identity is stable, but the local content model is extensively remodeled.

## Scope
Compared base R4 and R6 Encounter StructureDefinitions and relevant local terminology. Inherited base-artifact changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
Major themes are required status-code migration, Coding/CodeableConcept/CodeableReference reshaping, path renames/moves, removal of inline histories and diagnosis rank, and R6-to-R4 policies for new workflow fields.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `Encounter.status`, `Encounter.class`, `Encounter.period`, removed history backbones, participant/reason/diagnosis remodels, and CodeableReference adoption.

## Findings requiring human review
Review status mappings, class terminology, removed histories, participant constraints, ImmunizationRecommendation reasons, Procedure/rank diagnoses, and serviceType references.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Some R6 additions are forward-compatible, but many remodels could have used deprecated aliases or official ConceptMaps to reduce breakage.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: Encounter has high-impact local breaking changes despite stable identity. Top concerns are required status code changes, structural remodels for class/reason/diagnosis/participants/timing, and lossy R6-to-R4 conversion. Main uncertainty is official migration intent for histories and terminology.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Implement explicit transforms for status, class, actual/planned timing, admission, participant actor, reason, diagnosis, serviceType, and location form. Preserve removed history/rank data deliberately and define R6-to-R4 extension or rejection rules.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for StructureDefinition deltas and local complete status CodeSystems. Confidence is medium for terminology semantics and replacement intent because official diffs, narrative pages, and terminology expansions were not available.

findings.title: Required Encounter.status code set removed several R4 lifecycle states

oldState.summary: R4 status is mandatory code bound required to encounter-status|4.0.1, including arrived, triaged, onleave, and finished.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 status is mandatory code bound required to encounter-status|4.0.1, including arrived, triaged, onleave, and finished.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Compared local complete CodeSystem JSON files, not a terminology-server expansion.

newState.summary: R6 status remains mandatory required code, but the local CodeSystem omits arrived, triaged, onleave, and finished and adds on-hold, discharged, completed, and discontinued.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 status remains mandatory required code, but the local CodeSystem omits arrived, triaged, onleave, and finished and adds on-hold, discharged, completed, and discontinued.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 separates subject state and business workflow from lifecycle status.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Required binding validation rejects R4 Encounters using removed codes; R6-added statuses have no lossless R4 status code.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate encounter lifecycle from subject/business status.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated legacy status aliases while adding subjectStatus/businessStatus for the R6 distinctions.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal is reasonable: `arrived` and `triaged` fit subject state better than encounter lifecycle, while `completed`, `discharged`, and `discontinued` provide clearer lifecycle stages. A less-breaking base design exists for some codes, but keeping all old codes valid would materially weaken the semantic cleanup of a required modifier element.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best base alternative would retain deprecated R4 aliases such as `finished`, `onleave`, `arrived`, and `triaged` in the required value set while adding the new R6 codes and the new subject/business status elements. That would preserve R4 instances, but it is only partial because `arrived` and `triaged` would remain valid lifecycle statuses even though R6 is trying to separate subject state from encounter status. ConceptMaps and conversion rules are useful migration aids, not by themselves backward-compatible base designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old status values but leaves patient-state and lifecycle concepts mixed in a required modifier code.

evidence.detail: R4 required binding points to encounter-status|4.0.1.
R6 required binding points to encounter-status|6.0.0-ballot4.
Local CodeSystems show removed and added codes.

examples.examplesMd: Fragments illustrate status only; other Encounter fields also changed.

findings.narrativeMd: `Encounter.status` is still required and modifier, but several R4 codes are no longer legal. This is a high-risk enum, validator, and workflow migration issue.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with `status: arrived`, `triaged`, `onleave`, or `finished` can be valid in R4 and invalid in R6. R6 `discharged` and `discontinued` cannot be represented exactly in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create a status map. Likely mappings include `finished` to `completed` and `onleave` to `on-hold`; treat `arrived`/`triaged` as subjectStatus or businessStatus with local review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Deprecated aliases or a normative ConceptMap would have reduced breakage while preserving the cleaner R6 model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No official local R4-to-R6 status ConceptMap was found.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Encounter.status` remains mandatory and modifier, but the required code set no longer accepts several R4 lifecycle/status values. That is a direct validation break for central workflow data, and the migration is not purely mechanical for `arrived` and `triaged` because R6 moved that meaning toward subject/business status rather than the lifecycle status.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.status: 1..1 code, required encounter-status|4.0.1, modifier
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.status: 1..1 code, required encounter-status|6.0.0-ballot4, modifier
Local CodeSystems: R4 has arrived/triaged/onleave/finished; R6 instead has on-hold/discharged/completed/discontinued
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2 and trial-use status are neutral: they do not create a normative stability burden, but they also do not soften a required modifier status code used in routine Encounter workflows.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances using removed required-binding codes fail R6 validation; there is also R6-to-R4 loss for new R6 status codes.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept the R4 codes as deprecated aliases while adding subjectStatus/businessStatus and new lifecycle codes. The tradeoff is real because it keeps patient-state concepts mixed into a modifier lifecycle field, but the required-code break is important enough to revisit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies high bidirectional impact and a partial alternative; I put stronger action weight on the central required modifier code and expert-dependent mappings.

findings.title: Encounter.class changed from mandatory single Coding to optional repeating CodeableConcept

oldState.summary: R4 class is 1..1 Coding with extensible v3 ActEncounterCode binding.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 class is 1..1 Coding with extensible v3 ActEncounterCode binding.

newState.summary: R6 class is 0..* CodeableConcept with preferred encounter-class binding.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 class is 0..* CodeableConcept with preferred encounter-class binding.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The JSON shape changes from a single Coding object to an array of CodeableConcepts; R6 can omit or repeat class, which R4 cannot represent.

justification.inferredGoal: Support multiple and richer encounter classifications.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain R4 `class` as a deprecated Coding and add a separate repeatable CodeableConcept classification element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Supporting multiple richer encounter classifications is a plausible R6 goal, and normalizing on one repeatable `CodeableConcept` path avoids long-term ambiguity. The less-breaking option would preserve a very common R4 field, but it would leave R6 with two same-resource ways to represent encounter class.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `Encounter.class` as the R4 single `Coding` during a transition and add a new optional repeatable classification element for CodeableConcepts. That would accept existing R4 JSON, but implementations would need precedence and reconciliation rules when the old Coding and new concepts both appear, and producers might continue populating both indefinitely.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 data but creates duplicate classification representations and conflict rules.

examples.examplesMd: FHIR arrays are required for repeating R6 class.

findings.narrativeMd: `class` kept the same path but changed cardinality, datatype, and binding strength. Generated models and JSON serializers need explicit conversion.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Normal R4 `class` data is invalid as-is in R6. Valid R6 data with multiple class values, text-only concepts, or no class is not faithfully representable in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap the R4 Coding as `class[0].coding[0]`. For R6-to-R4 choose one coded class or preserve extras with extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 shape is expressive, but a deprecation window would have reduced breakage.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The R6 encounter-class ValueSet was referenced but not found as a local JSON file.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `Encounter.class` changes from a required single `Coding` to an optional repeating `CodeableConcept`, so ordinary R4 JSON and generated model properties need conversion. The R6 goal of supporting multiple, richer classifications is coherent, and preserving the R4 shape would likely require duplicate classification fields or precedence rules.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.class: 1..1 Coding, extensible v3-ActEncounterCode
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.class: 0..* CodeableConcept, preferred encounter-class
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the judgment rests on the concrete wire-shape and codegen break rather than maturity pressure.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 single Coding object is not the R6 repeating CodeableConcept array shape; SDK and FHIRPath users also see a runtime/API/codegen change.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would retain the old single Coding and add a new repeatable classification element. That would preserve R4 instances but creates duplicate encounter-class representations and conflict handling when both are populated.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing high-impact and partial-alternative assessment is directionally right, though under this rubric the break appears proportionate.

findings.title: Encounter.period was replaced by Encounter.actualPeriod and planned dates were added

oldState.summary: R4 uses 0..1 Period `period` for start/end time.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 uses 0..1 Period `period` for start/end time.

newState.summary: R6 uses 0..1 Period `actualPeriod` and adds plannedStartDate/plannedEndDate dateTimes.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses 0..1 Period `actualPeriod` and adds plannedStartDate/plannedEndDate dateTimes.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 `period` is an unknown R6 element unless renamed; R6 planned dates have no R4 base slot.

justification.inferredGoal: Separate actual and planned encounter timing.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `period` as the actual encounter period and add optional plannedStartDate/plannedEndDate.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Separating actual and planned timing is useful, but the breaking rename from `period` to `actualPeriod` was not necessary to achieve that goal. R6 could have clarified that the existing `period` means actual time and added planned date fields without invalidating R4 instances.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base design would retain `Encounter.period` with updated wording such as "actual start and end time" and add the planned date elements beside it. This preserves nearly all R4 data and FHIRPath/codegen paths. The main tradeoff is a nonideal element name, which is modest compared with a direct path break.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old instances with low cost, but keeps a less explicit historical name for actual timing.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: Timing is now explicit as actual versus planned. Existing stores, search logic, and transforms using `Encounter.period` must change.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing `period` fail strict R6 validation. R6 planned dates cannot be represented in base R4 without extensions or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename `period` to `actualPeriod`; do not map planned dates into R4 period unless local policy intentionally treats planned time as actual.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Clarity improved, but retaining `period` with clarified semantics would have been less disruptive.

freshReview.narrativeMd: This is mostly a path rename from `period` to `actualPeriod` while the type and cardinality remain `0..1 Period`; planned dates are additive. R4 instances and code using `Encounter.period` break even though R6 could have clarified the old element as the actual period and added planned fields beside it.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.period: 0..1 Period, start and end time of the encounter
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.actualPeriod: 0..1 Period, actual start and end time
R6 StructureDefinition adds Encounter.plannedStartDate and Encounter.plannedEndDate
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; it does not by itself make the rename unacceptable, but it leaves the low-cost compatibility alternative decisive.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: `period` is not an R6 Encounter element; generated APIs, FHIRPath, and stored column mappings also break on the renamed path.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. Keeping `period` with clarified actual-period wording and adding optional planned date elements would meet the apparent R6 goal with little cost beyond a less explicit legacy name.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly treats this as a high-confidence avoidable path break with a strong less-breaking alternative.

findings.title: statusHistory and classHistory were removed from Encounter

oldState.summary: R4 has repeating statusHistory and classHistory backbones with status/class and period children.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has repeating statusHistory and classHistory backbones with status/class and period children.

newState.summary: R6 Encounter has no statusHistory or classHistory elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 Encounter has no statusHistory or classHistory elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any populated inline history backbone is an unknown element in R6; no equivalent local Encounter element exists.

justification.inferredGoal: Move historical state/class data out of current Encounter.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep statusHistory/classHistory as deprecated inline histories until the external history model is clearly available.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The apparent R6 goal of moving historical state out of the current Encounter is plausible, and R6 comments mention EncounterHistory for historical business statuses. However, the local package evidence did not include an EncounterHistory StructureDefinition or official migration guidance, so the proportionality of fully removing the inline R4 histories cannot be confidently assessed.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain the R4 `statusHistory` and `classHistory` backbones as deprecated compatibility fields while adding or documenting the preferred external history model. That is only a partial alternative because it perpetuates large Encounter resources and duplicate historical representations, especially if EncounterHistory or resource version history is intended to become the authoritative location.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves historical data but can bloat Encounter and duplicate EncounterHistory or resource-version history.

evidence.detail: R6 comments mention EncounterHistory for historical business statuses.
evidence.quote: Historical businessStatuses should be captured in EncounterHistory

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 allowed inline lifecycle/class histories. R6 removes those slots, creating both validation failures and possible historical data loss.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with either history backbone are R6-invalid. R6 has no local inline replacement; down-stream preservation likely needs external history, extensions, or version history.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory and preserve history intentionally. Do not drop histories silently; map to an official replacement if one is available outside the local package.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Removal may reduce duplicated history, but a deprecation period would have been safer.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: No StructureDefinition-EncounterHistory.json was present in the local R6 package.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 inline `statusHistory` and `classHistory` backbones disappear from R6 Encounter. That can reject old instances and lose audit/workflow transition data; the local R6 package did not contain an `EncounterHistory` StructureDefinition despite comments pointing historical business status there.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition defines Encounter.statusHistory and Encounter.classHistory as 0..* BackboneElement
R6 Encounter snapshot omits statusHistory and classHistory
R6 Encounter.businessStatus comment says historical businessStatuses should be captured in EncounterHistory
R6 package index and package files checked: no EncounterHistory StructureDefinition found
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but history of status/class transitions has credible operational and audit value, so maturity does not make removal harmless.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 instances with either inline history contain elements not accepted by R6; migration may also be lossy without a concrete replacement.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design would retain deprecated inline histories while documenting or adding the preferred external history model. The tradeoff is larger Encounter resources and duplicate history representations, but the replacement was not evident in the supplied local package.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report identifies the hard break and partial alternative; I treat the absent local replacement as enough for Revisit rather than leaving the proportionality merely unresolved.

findings.title: hospitalization was renamed to admission and selected children moved to Encounter root

oldState.summary: R4 admission/discharge details are under 0..1 `hospitalization`; dietPreference, specialArrangement, and specialCourtesy are children.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 admission/discharge details are under 0..1 `hospitalization`; dietPreference, specialArrangement, and specialCourtesy are children.

newState.summary: R6 uses 0..1 `admission`; dietPreference, specialArrangement, and specialCourtesy are top-level Encounter elements.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses 0..1 `admission`; dietPreference, specialArrangement, and specialCourtesy are top-level Encounter elements.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old paths are invalid in R6; most content is transformable but not by a simple parent rename.

justification.inferredGoal: Use broader admission terminology and make preferences apply to Encounter beyond admission.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `hospitalization` and old nested preference children while adding the new admission/root-level shape.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Renaming the backbone to `admission` and promoting preferences that apply to the whole Encounter are reasonable model clarifications. A compatibility alias could reduce breakage, but preserving both the old nested structure and the new root-level preference elements would create persistent duplicate locations.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking base design would accept `hospitalization` as a deprecated alias for `admission` and continue accepting nested diet, special-arrangement, and special-courtesy data while introducing the R6 root elements. That would preserve R4 instances, but implementations would need to reconcile old nested values with new root-level values and decide which representation controls when they diverge.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids old-path rejection but creates duplicate admission and preference locations with consistency risk.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: The hospitalization/admission change affects nested data. Some children stay under the renamed backbone; others are promoted.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with `hospitalization` are invalid in R6. R6 root-level preferences may not always mean admission-specific preferences when mapped back to R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map admission-specific children under `admission`; promote diet/special-arrangement/special-courtesy to root.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated alias would have reduced breakage but created duplicate locations.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `hospitalization` becomes `admission`, and several preference/courtesy children are promoted to Encounter root. This breaks old paths, but most content has an obvious target and the R6 naming/scope cleanup is reasonable.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.hospitalization: 0..1 BackboneElement
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.admission: 0..1 BackboneElement
R6 StructureDefinition promotes dietPreference, specialArrangement, and specialCourtesy to root-level Encounter elements
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the optional and mostly mechanically transformable nature of this path limits the concern.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 `hospitalization` and nested preference paths are not valid R6 paths without restructuring.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would keep `hospitalization` as a deprecated alias and continue accepting nested preference fields. That would preserve R4 JSON but creates duplicate admission/preference locations and consistency rules.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly finds a hard break and partial alternative, but its overall High impact seems overstated for a mostly mechanical optional-path migration.

findings.title: participant.individual was renamed to actor and target types expanded

oldState.summary: R4 participant.individual is 0..1 Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or RelatedPerson.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 participant.individual is 0..1 Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or RelatedPerson.

newState.summary: R6 participant.actor is 0..1 Reference to Patient, Group, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, or HealthcareService.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 participant.actor is 0..1 Reference to Patient, Group, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, or HealthcareService.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 participant.individual is unknown in R6; R6 actor can reference resource types not allowed in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent participants that are not just individual people.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `participant.individual` and broaden its definition and target profiles to cover the R6 actor domain.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The goal of allowing non-practitioner participants is reasonable, and `actor` is a clearer name. Still, the base R6 goal could largely have been met by retaining the R4 path and broadening its allowed targets and definition, so the path break is not clearly necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would keep `Encounter.participant.individual` and update its definition to mean the participating person, patient/group, device, or service, with the expanded R6 target set. This would preserve R4 instances and avoid duplicate representations. The cost is a misleading legacy name, especially for non-individual actors, but FHIR could mitigate that with clearer definitions and deprecation guidance rather than changing the wire path.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves R4 paths with no duplicate field, but leaves an awkward name for devices, groups, and services.

evidence.detail: R6 target set adds Patient, Group, Device, HealthcareService.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: Participant actor identity changed path and meaning. Codegen, FHIRPath, and reference validation need updating.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old participant.individual data is invalid until renamed. Valid R6 Patient/Group/Device/HealthcareService actors cannot be represented in R4 participant.individual.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename individual to actor; for down-conversion only map Practitioner, PractitionerRole, and RelatedPerson directly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The rename is justified by semantics but a deprecated alias would have eased migration.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `participant.individual` was renamed to `participant.actor` while also broadening allowed targets. The target expansion is useful, but the wire-path break appears avoidable because the old path could have been retained with an updated definition and broader target list.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.participant.individual: Reference to Practitioner, PractitionerRole, or RelatedPerson
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.participant.actor: Reference to Patient, Group, RelatedPerson, Practitioner, PractitionerRole, Device, or HealthcareService
R6 participant.actor definition explicitly covers individual, device, or service participation
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the common participant actor path and low-cost compatibility option drive the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 participant.individual is not an R6 element; new R6 actor targets also create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Yes. R6 could have kept `participant.individual` and broadened its target profiles and prose. The cost is an awkward legacy name for devices, groups, and services, but it avoids duplicate fields and preserves old instances.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies high impact and a plausible less-breaking base design.

findings.title: R6 adds error constraints on participant actor/type combinations

oldState.summary: R4 participant had no local Encounter-specific constraints.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 participant had no local Encounter-specific constraints.

newState.summary: R6 adds enc-1 requiring actor or type and enc-2 prohibiting type for Patient/Group actors.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 adds enc-1 requiring actor or type and enc-2 prohibiting type for Patient/Group actors.

constraints.human: A type must be provided when no explicit actor is specified
A type cannot be provided for a patient or group participant
constraints.expression: actor.exists(resolve() is Patient or resolve() is Group) implies type.exists().not()

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 participant repetitions with only period/extensions can become invalid; enc-2 also constrains valid R6 patient/group actor data.

justification.inferredGoal: Make participant entries meaningful and avoid role-typing subject actors.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Introduce enc-1/enc-2 as warnings or profile constraints before making them base errors.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The constraints serve a real data-quality goal: participant entries should identify an actor or role, and patient/group actors should not be role-typed as if they were other participants. A warning or profile-first rollout would be less disruptive, but it would not enforce the same invariant for all base-valid R6 Encounter data.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The less-breaking alternative would make these rules best-practice warnings or move them to profiles during a transition. That would preserve R4 participant repetitions that contain only timing or extensions, but it is only partial because base R6 would still allow participant records that are hard to interpret or semantically misleading.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces validation breakage but leaves ambiguous or misleading participant entries base-valid.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: The new participant invariants are local Encounter validation rules, not inherited base rules.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A participant with only `period` can be R4-valid but R6-invalid. Enforcement of the Patient/Group rule depends on reference resolution.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Ensure each participant has actor or type; remove type from Patient/Group actor entries or use another representation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A warning-first approach would have been less breaking but less strict.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Operational impact of enc-2 depends on validator resolve() behavior.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R6 adds error-level participant invariants requiring either an actor or type and disallowing type for Patient/Group actors. This can reject some R4-valid sparse participant repetitions, but those repetitions are ambiguous, and the new constraints enforce a reasonable minimum meaning.
keyEvidence: R4 Encounter.participant has no local Encounter-specific constraints beyond inherited ele-1
R6 Encounter.participant adds enc-1: actor.exists() or type.exists()
R6 Encounter.participant adds enc-2: Patient/Group actor implies type does not exist
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the break affects a narrower and often low-information participant shape rather than a core required field.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 participant containing only period/extensions can become R6-invalid; enc-2 also constrains new R6 Patient/Group participant usage.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would introduce these rules as warnings or profile constraints first. That reduces validation breakage but leaves ambiguous base Encounter participant entries valid.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report's medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment matches the fresh review.

findings.title: reasonCode and reasonReference were merged into Encounter.reason.value CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 has separate repeating reasonCode CodeableConcept and reasonReference Reference targets Condition, Procedure, Observation, ImmunizationRecommendation.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has separate repeating reasonCode CodeableConcept and reasonReference Reference targets Condition, Procedure, Observation, ImmunizationRecommendation.

newState.summary: R6 has repeating reason backbone with reason.use and reason.value CodeableReference targets Condition, DiagnosticReport, Observation, Procedure.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 has repeating reason backbone with reason.use and reason.value CodeableReference targets Condition, DiagnosticReport, Observation, Procedure.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old top-level reason paths are invalid in R6; R4 ImmunizationRecommendation references and R6 DiagnosticReport/use data need policy.

justification.inferredGoal: Unify coded and referenced reasons and add reason-use classification.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` while adding `reason.value` CodeableReference and `reason.use`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Unifying coded and referenced reasons and adding reason-use classification is a reasonable R6 modeling goal. The alias approach would preserve old instances, but it would leave multiple same-resource representations of the reason for the encounter and complicate safety-relevant interpretation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could keep `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` as deprecated aliases while adding the new `reason` backbone for CodeableReference values and use codes. That is only a partial alternative: clients would need to merge old and new reason lists, handle duplicate facts, and resolve conflicts. It also would not fully solve target changes such as the dropped ImmunizationRecommendation target and added DiagnosticReport target.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old reason paths but risks duplicate or conflicting reason lists for a clinically important field.

evidence.detail: R4 has separate top-level reason elements.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: Reasons are now grouped in a backbone rather than split across two top-level lists.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 reasonCode/reasonReference instances are R6-invalid until reshaped. R6 reason.use and DiagnosticReport references are not native R4 fields; R4 ImmunizationRecommendation references are no longer a listed target.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move codes to `reason.value.concept` and references to `reason.value.reference`; review ImmunizationRecommendation and use semantics manually.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A transitional alias strategy would have reduced migration risk.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4's separate `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` lists become an R6 `reason` backbone with `reason.value` CodeableReference and optional `reason.use`. This is a real path and model break, and ImmunizationRecommendation references need review, but the unified reason model is coherent and aliasing the old lists would create duplicate clinical reason representations.

R4 StructureDefinition Encounter.reasonReference: 0..* Reference to Condition, Procedure, Observation, or ImmunizationRecommendation
R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.reason.value: 0..* CodeableReference to Condition, DiagnosticReport, Observation, or Procedure

freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; the clinical importance of reasons raises migration care, but not enough to outweigh the coherent consolidation goal.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: old top-level reasonCode/reasonReference fields are not valid R6 paths; target changes create additional mapping review.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would retain deprecated `reasonCode` and `reasonReference` and keep the old ImmunizationRecommendation target while adding the new backbone. That preserves more R4 data but creates duplicate reason lists, merge rules, and conflict risks.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing report correctly identifies high impact and only a partial less-breaking alternative; the fresh judgment treats the change as proportionate.

findings.title: Diagnosis condition/use/rank were remodeled

oldState.summary: R4 diagnosis.condition is 1..1 Reference to Condition or Procedure; use is 0..1 diagnosis-role; rank is 0..1 positiveInt.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 diagnosis.condition is 1..1 Reference to Condition or Procedure; use is 0..1 diagnosis-role; rank is 0..1 positiveInt.

newState.summary: R6 diagnosis.condition is 0..* CodeableReference to Condition with example condition-code binding; use is 0..* encounter-diagnosis-use; rank is removed.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 diagnosis.condition is 0..* CodeableReference to Condition with example condition-code binding; use is 0..* encounter-diagnosis-use; rank is removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 diagnosis entries must be reshaped; Procedure references and rank have no direct R6 diagnosis location.

justification.inferredGoal: Represent coded diagnoses/Condition references and separate billing ranking elsewhere.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Procedure target and rank as deprecated compatibility content while adding CodeableReference Condition support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal appears to narrow Encounter diagnosis to coded diagnoses or Condition references and move billing rank concerns to Account, which is a reasonable cleanup. The break remains high impact, especially for Procedure references and rank, but retaining all old content would undermine the clearer division between diagnoses, reasons/procedures, and billing-account ranking.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could retain `diagnosis.rank` and the Procedure target as deprecated compatibility features while allowing repeatable CodeableReference(Condition) values. This would preserve R4 instances, but it is only partial because rank would compete with Account-based billing diagnosis ranking, and Procedure-as-diagnosis would overlap with reason/procedure representations. Conversion extensions are mitigation, not a base-design alternative.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old billing/procedure data but duplicates newer Condition, reason, and Account-based diagnosis semantics.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: Diagnosis migration is a high-impact semantic and billing issue, not just a datatype wrapper.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 Procedure diagnoses are invalid as R6 diagnosis.condition. R4 rank is lost unless preserved elsewhere. R6 coded or multiple diagnoses are not R4-representable without choices/extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map Condition references to CodeableReference.reference; decide how to handle Procedure and rank, possibly through reason, Account, or extensions.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A less-breaking design would retain rank/Procedure as deprecated fields for one release.

freshReview.narrativeMd: Encounter diagnosis changed substantially: `condition` is no longer a required single Reference that can point to Procedure, it is repeatable CodeableReference to Condition only; `use` repeats with a new value set; `rank` is removed. Procedure diagnoses and billing rank are business- and billing-relevant, and moving that meaning elsewhere requires expert policy rather than a simple wrapper transform.
keyEvidence: R4 Encounter.diagnosis.condition: 1..1 Reference to Condition or Procedure
R4 Encounter.diagnosis.rank: 0..1 positiveInt
R6 Encounter.diagnosis.condition: 0..* CodeableReference targeting Condition only
R6 Encounter.diagnosis comment says billing diagnoses are recorded in Account where they can be ranked
R6 Encounter snapshot has no diagnosis.rank
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral, but diagnosis and billing rank have credible clinical/business consequences, so the lossy expert-dependent migration remains concerning.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: R4 diagnosis entries with required Reference shape, Procedure targets, or rank are not directly valid in R6; R6 coded/multiple diagnoses also create R6-to-R4 loss.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial less-breaking design could keep Procedure targets and `rank` as deprecated compatibility features while adding CodeableReference(Condition). The tradeoff is overlap with cleaner R6 diagnosis, reason, and Account-based billing semantics, but rank/procedure loss is significant enough to revisit.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly marks high impact and a partial alternative; I give more weight to billing/rank and Procedure loss and judge the design should be revisited.

findings.title: serviceType changed from CodeableConcept to repeating CodeableReference(HealthcareService)

newState.narrativeMd: R6 serviceType is 0..* CodeableReference targeting HealthcareService.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Populated R4 serviceType must be wrapped into an R6 array of CodeableReference; R6 HealthcareService references are not native R4 serviceType.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow service type as either code or HealthcareService reference and allow multiples.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep CodeableConcept `serviceType` and add a separate optional HealthcareService reference element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing service type to be represented either as a concept or a HealthcareService reference, and allowing multiple values, is a reasonable R6 goal. A sibling reference field would avoid rejecting R4 JSON, but it would not provide a single normalized serviceType representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would keep R4 `serviceType` as CodeableConcept, optionally make it repeatable, and add a separate HealthcareService reference element. That would preserve old instances and support references, but implementations would need to search and reconcile both fields and handle cases where a coded type and referenced HealthcareService disagree.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old coded service types but splits one service-type fact across concept and reference fields.

examples.examplesMd: No complete instance example supplied; finding is based on computable StructureDefinition deltas.

findings.narrativeMd: `serviceType` keeps its name but not its wire shape.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 CodeableConcept serviceType is invalid as-is in R6. R6 references/multiple values cannot be losslessly represented in R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap old values as `serviceType[].concept`; for reverse conversion derive one concept or use an extension for references.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A parallel reference element would have been more compatible but less unified.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `serviceType` keeps its name but changes from a single CodeableConcept to repeating CodeableReference(HealthcareService). Existing coded service types need wrapping, and R6 references/multiples need down-conversion policy, but the R6 model cleanly supports both coded and referenced services.

R6 StructureDefinition Encounter.serviceType: 0..* CodeableReference targeting HealthcareService, example service-type
freshReview.fmmEffect: Supplied R4 FMM 2/trial-use is neutral; this optional example-bound field has real codegen impact but a limited base compatibility burden.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid: an R4 CodeableConcept value is not the R6 repeating CodeableReference shape; R6 HealthcareService references and multiple entries are not lossless in R4.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A partial alternative would keep CodeableConcept serviceType and add a separate HealthcareService reference field. That preserves R4 instances but splits one service-type concept across two fields and requires reconciliation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree: the existing medium-impact and partial-alternative assessment is appropriate.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old path is unknown in R6; type/cardinality are otherwise stable and mapping is direct.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a clearer/general name for location form.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `location.physicalType` and update its wording/value set to cover the R6 form concept.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 `form` name is cleaner and broader, but the element's type and cardinality are unchanged and the old field already carried the same basic location-form fact. The supplied evidence does not show that changing the wire path was necessary.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design would retain `Encounter.location.physicalType` and clarify its definition to include bed, room, ward, virtual, or other form values, possibly with the updated `location-form` binding. This preserves R4 instances with only modest naming cost; an alias would also work but would add duplicate paths.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids the path break with low cost, but keeps a narrower legacy element name.

findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Rename the element and keep codes.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `location.physicalType` was renamed to `location.form` while remaining a `0..1 CodeableConcept` for the location form/level. This is a direct path break with little apparent model payoff; the old name could have been retained with updated wording and binding.
